summary: EtherHiding loader in babel.config.cjs fetches and executes attacker-controlled code
details: babel.config.cjs ships a heavily obfuscated IIFE appended to an otherwise ordinary Babel preset config. The obfuscated code queries public Ethereum RPC endpoints (eth.drpc.org, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io, 1rpc.io/eth, and the Etherscan API) for transactions involving a hardcoded attacker address, decodes IPv4 addresses out of transaction byte fields to derive C2 hosts, fetches an XOR-encrypted JavaScript payload from those hosts over plain HTTP (:80 and:443), decrypts it, and executes it by both eval() and spawn('node', ['-e', header+payload], {detached: true, stdio: 'ignore', windowsHide: true}).unref(). The detached hidden Node process runs independently of the parent with globals (_V, _H, _H2, _t_u, _t_s) seeded with C2 URLs, giving the operator persistent code execution on any developer machine that loads this Babel config (e.g. via Babel/Jest while working with the package). Using on-chain lookups to resolve C2 addresses lets the operator rotate infrastructure without republishing the package. String-array obfuscation of RPC hostnames, spawn/eval sinks, and the XOR routine is used to conceal these behaviors in a file that has no legitimate reason to contain runtime code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
